🏆 User of the Week

Building a Competitive Intelligence Engine at SAP Concur

Lauren Cochrane is leading the rollout of Crayon for competitive intelligence and piloting Clozd for win-loss analysis at SAP Concur. The goal? An AI-driven centralized competitive intelligence engine that serves sales, marketing, and product teams.

Why This Matters

Lauren's team was using Valona (CI news tracking) and Anova (win-loss) — both underperforming, lacking AI and automation. The evaluation surfaced key patterns:

  • Best-of-breed beats all-in-one: Crayon + Clozd outperformed Klue
  • Pricing models matter: Crayon's unlimited users vs. Klue's 3,000-seat model
  • Native multilingual: Clozd's $300/interview vs. Klue's $500 for non-English
  • Integration is key: Clozd has native Crayon integration

🧪 From the Lab

Our Google Antigravity Beta Test

SAP is one of the early enterprise testers of Google Antigravity — Google's new "agent-first" IDE powered by Gemini 3. I'm our team's beta representative, and this week we hit our first real friction point.

🔧 The Issue

When running on Windows (via WSL2), the tool's "strict mode" enforces a sandbox that blocks all network access. You can't even run pip install. Mac users have toggle options; Windows users don't.

Enterprise AI tooling is moving fast, but the security/usability tradeoff is real. We're working with Google to find a middle ground. Stay tuned.

📉 Market Signal

The SaaS Reckoning Is Here

Salesforce is down 37% YTD. Snowflake 44%. Adobe 35%. The narrative? AI copilots and agents are "compressing growth and pricing power."

Meanwhile, HubSpot shifted to outcome-based pricing. Their AI agents now cost $0.50 per resolved conversation. Pay for results, not usage.
